newsitem.title: POLAND: Late orders dent zloty gains, one-day depos ease.
newsitem.headline: Late orders dent zloty gains, one-day depos ease.

text.p: The zloty held on to early gains against the currency basket despite late currency buying orders which depressed the Polish currency just before close.

Dealers said the market sentiment was slightly bullish early in the day as expected currency buying orders failed to materialise, but that the trend had reversed in active trade late in the trading session.

"The zloty drifted up against the basket for most of the day but late currency-buying orders, likely coming from a client, took the wind from the zloty's sails," said Pawel Gajewski of Creditanstalt in Warsaw.
The zloty closed stronger against the basket of currencies at 1.88/1.76 percent below the trading band centre, called the parity rate, against Monday's close at 1.76/1.70 percent.
It was at 2.8055/70 to the dollar, up from 2.8100/10 on Monday and at 1.8393/19 to the mark, down from 1.8390/05.
Dealers said banks were keeping short currency positions because of attractive one-day rates on the Polish money market.

"Many are keeping foreign currency positions short because Polish overnight rates are still high and more favourable than foreign currency deposits amid stable dollar/mark," said one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw.

At today's 14-day reverse repo operation the National Bank of Poland (NBP) rejected all 266 million zlotys of bids, sending a sinal to the market that it would like to see one-day deposit rates ease, dealers said.

Dealers said that if the NBP would remain consistant in keeping the 14-day drainage level around 19.13 percent amid current one-day rates of between 20 and 21.5 percent, call money depos would be forced to come down soon.
"The present 21.50 percent is too much and one-day depos will fall, but I don't know whether they will dip as far as the reverse-repo level," said Adam Gadomski of Bank Handlowy SA.
Overnight rates closed at 19.95/21.05 percent, down from Monday's close at 21.45/21.50 and tomorrow/next rates at 20.30/21.20 percent, also down from 21.00/21.45 yesterday.
In secondary T-bill trade 52-week T-bills sold on Monday with an average yield of 19.43 percent were traded around 19.40 percent, while 342-day paper was traded around 19.38 percent.
Yields of 26-week T-bills held flat at primary auction levels of 19.09 percent.
